analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. It adds changelog.d/fused-causal-prefill-attention.md (lines 1-5), one table row in docs/architecture/inference.md (head line 1090) and one env-var row in docs/reference/configuration.md (head line 397). The rows document a default-on fused causal SDPA prefill path for eligible full-attention chunks, with DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL=0 as the rollback. The variable is read once per process and is not forwarded to LaunchAgents.

No executable code, wire contract, key handling, attestation or App Attest authorization, or cache-storage and crypto logic changes in the supplied evidence. The documented path is a compute-kernel choice inside the provider process (TB-007). It does not touch cacheSalt scoping, HMAC lookup tags, DBK3 AAD, the TTL or the KEK handling (T-041). The TTFT hit/miss oracle (SEC-035) is accepted in kind and unchanged. The env knob is operator-local config (TB-003, ADV-001), the same class as the other DARKBLOOM_CBV2_* knobs. It is not forwarded to the LaunchAgent, so the installed provider keeps the default.

The Swift implementation (AttentionV1.swift `usesFusedCausalPrefill`, PagedLayerCache.swift `prefillAttend`) is not in the supplied evidence. The fused-mask correctness, the exclusion of live packed paged KV, and cross-request isolation (T-028/T-041) are unverified contracts and not findings. Any companion code review should check causal offsets for prefix-cache-restored chunks, packed batch row isolation, and prefill memory admission with the changed workspace. The changelog notes numerical differences within bf16 rounding on M5 and unmeasured models, which is a correctness and qualification caveat only. I found no security regression from the docs alone, and the integration source replay was incomplete, with 18 omitted units.
